sheets.name: How to
values: How to: the volunteer kiosk sheet

Short how-tos for the jobs staff do in this spreadsheet. The kiosk writes this tab and rewrites it whenever the kiosk is updated, so changes made here won't last; to suggest a change, tell the kiosk's developers.
Hover over a column header on the Log or the Flags tab to see what that column holds; the same notes are at the end of this tab. On the Settings tab, the What it does column explains each setting.
Problems with the kiosk
Before you start

Use the Kiosk admin menu in a browser signed in to just one Google account, the shared kiosk account. With two accounts signed in, its windows can fail with a PERMISSION_DENIED error; a private (incognito) window signed in to the kiosk account fixes it.
Every save asks for your initials (1 to 5 letters), so the sheet shows who did what.
A menu window stops working after 30 minutes. Close it and open the menu again.
If a save is refused, the window says why and keeps what you typed.
Review flags

A flag is something the kiosk wants a person to look at: a time far from when the volunteer tapped, a very long shift, a shift the nightly auto clock-out closed, a name Import past hours couldn't match or a paper shift it brought in for a day the volunteer also has a kiosk shift, or a problem the morning Log check found.
1. Open the Flags tab, then Data > Change view > Flags: Unreviewed. It shows the flags nobody has ticked yet, newest first.
2. Read the Reason. To find the shift on the Log, copy its Shift ID, open the Log, press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) and paste.
3. Fix the shift if it needs it (see below), or leave it if it's fine.
4. Tick Reviewed, type your initials in Reviewed By, and add a note in Notes if there's something to say. The flag leaves the view.

Fixing a shift doesn't tick its flag: tick it yourself. A flag the morning Log check raised (Source: log check) comes back if you delete its row while the problem is still on the Log; other flags don't come back.
Fix a sign-out (someone forgot to check out)
1. Kiosk admin > Fix a sign-out…
2. Pick the shift from the list of open shifts. Type part of the name to search.
3. Enter the time they left (it goes on the shift's own date), a note if you like, and your initials. Press Save.
If the check-in time itself is wrong or can't be read, fix it on the Log first, then come back here.
Add a shift (someone forgot to check in and out)
1. Kiosk admin > Add a shift…
2. Search for the volunteer. People who share a name show their Profiles row and the last four digits of their phone, so you can tell them apart.
3. Pick the date, enter the check-in and check-out times they gave you, a note if you like, and your initials. Press Save.
If they still have an open shift that day, close it with Kiosk admin > Fix a sign-out… first.
Remove a shift (a row that shouldn't be there)
1. Kiosk admin > Remove a shift…
2. Paste the shift's Shift ID, or pick the volunteer and the date, then press Find.
3. Pick the row and check its details show the right shift.
4. Type a reason and your initials. Press Save.
The row moves to the Removed shifts tab, so nothing is lost, and its flags are ticked. A row with no Shift ID can't be removed this way: delete it on the Log by hand.
Restore a shift (put a removed row back)
1. Kiosk admin > Restore a shift…
2. Find the row in the list, newest first; type to search. Each row shows who removed it, when and why.
3. Type your initials and press Save. The row goes back at the bottom of the Log.
The Hours tab shows an added, fixed, removed or restored shift after its next refresh: about 5 AM, or now with Kiosk admin > Refresh Hours.
Make an hours report
1. Kiosk admin > Hours report…
2. Choose the period: Month, Quarter, Year, Date range or All time. Then choose the month, quarter or year, or type the From and To dates.
3. Type your initials and press Make report.

4. The report goes on a new tab named for the period, such as Report 2026-11, Report 2026-Q4, Report 2026, Report 2026-03-15 to 2026-06-30 or Report all time. The window then shows Download CSV and Download PDF links for that tab.
The report's dollar figure uses Volunteer hour value on the Settings tab. Making the same report again makes a second tab; delete old report tabs when you're done with them.
Email volunteers their hours

Each volunteer you tick gets one email with their hours for the month, the year so far and all time, sent to the email on their Volunteer Profiles row from an address that can't take replies. It names who to contact about their hours from Hours email contact on the Settings tab, so type that first: while it's blank, nothing can be sent.
1. Kiosk admin > Email hours…
2. Choose this month or last month. For last month, all three totals are as of that month's last day.
3. Tick Attach all shifts if they should also get a spreadsheet file of every shift they have.

4. Tick the volunteers. Type part of a name to search; Tick all shown with the search empty ticks everyone. Volunteers who asked on the tablet arrive ticked and marked Requested and the date (see Hours requests from the tablet).

5. Press Preview. Check each volunteer's address, hours and the warnings under Check before sending. A volunteer with a problem, such as no email on their Profiles row, is left out and the problem says where to fix it.
6. Type your initials and press Send email. The list then says, for each volunteer, sent, failed or not sent and why.

One failure doesn't stop the rest. Every volunteer a send handles gets a row on the Hours emails tab with the result. Bounces go to the inbox of the account you're signed in as. To send again, press Preview again.
Hours requests from the tablet

Hours requests on the Settings tab decides whether volunteers can ask for their hours on the tablet. Off, the default, hides the Request my hours link on the tablet's welcome screen. Approve shows it and leaves each request for you to send. Auto shows it and the kiosk emails each request by itself, about every 15 minutes.

A volunteer taps the link, finds their name, and taps Send on the screen that follows. That only records a request on the Hours requests tab, one open request per volunteer. Nothing on that path checks anyone in or out. The tablet never shows an email address: the email goes to the Email cell of the volunteer's Volunteer Profiles row, as from Email hours.
1. Kiosk admin > Email hours… Volunteers who asked are ticked and marked Requested and the date. In Auto only held and overdue requests are ticked, since Auto sends the rest.

2. A held request says why, such as no email on their Profiles row, and the preview repeats it. Fix that, then Preview and send as usual. A sent email marks the request sent on the Hours requests tab.
3. To drop a request without sending, such as a repeat or someone who has left, type closed in its Status on the Hours requests tab and your initials in Done by.

In Auto, each email leaves out two kinds of shift and says how many are waiting for staff review: a shift whose Flags row isn't ticked Reviewed (tick it once you have checked the shift), and a shift still open (close it with Kiosk admin > Fix a sign-out…). A deleted Flags row counts as reviewed, so delete only flags you have looked at.

A volunteer who asks while checked in is emailed after they check out. Checked in means as the tablet shows it: until they check out, or until Auto clock-out after hours has passed since they checked in. One still checked in at 6:00 AM is held: close the shift with Kiosk admin > Fix a sign-out…, then send from Email hours.
Auto sends one email a week at most to each volunteer and 50 a day in all. A request past either limit is held for you. Auto never retries a held request.

A request still waiting in Auto a day after it was made is overdue: Email hours ticks it and labels it overdue. That is how a stopped hours request job shows. Hours requests last run on the Settings tab says when the job last sent, held or failed; a run with nothing to do writes nothing, so an old time there is normal.

Auto can't catch a believable fake shift: someone who taps in and out at real times without volunteering makes a normal row. It also counts a shift added with Add a shift or typed by hand, a hand edit the nightly Log check hasn't flagged yet, and a flag ticked Reviewed without anyone looking. Use Approve if a person should check every email.

If you send to a volunteer Auto is emailing at the same moment, they may get two emails, and the message line says so. Automatic emails are on the Hours emails tab with Sent by auto. Auto is installed by whoever looks after the kiosk; ask them if requests go overdue.
The weekly flags email

Once a week the kiosk can email a short list of new and unreviewed flags. It sends only when there is something to report: a flag raised in the last 7 days, a flag nobody has ticked Reviewed, or a nightly auto clock-out that hasn't run for over 2 days or has never run.
1. On the Settings tab, type the addresses in the Value of Flags email to.
2. Change Flags email day and Flags email hour (Central time) if Monday at 8 AM doesn't suit.

3. Set Flags email to On. The kiosk checks once an hour. If Flags email last run is blank, unreadable or older than the last time that day and hour came round, the next hourly check runs, whatever the day. After that a check runs once a week, at the first hourly check on or after that day and hour. A check with nothing to report sends nothing and writes "nothing to send" in Flags email last run.

Changing the day or hour takes effect at once: if the new day and hour have come round since the last check, a check runs within the hour. To stop the email, set Flags email to Off. To check this week again, clear the Value of Flags email last run: the next hourly check runs, and sends if there is anything to report.

With Hours requests on, the email also counts the hours emails Auto sent or tried in the last 7 days, and the hours requests waiting for you; either alone makes it send. With Flags email Off, see the Hours emails tab and Email hours instead.
Change a setting
1. Open the Settings tab and find the setting in the Setting column. Its What it does column says what it does and what to type.
2. Type the new value in the Value column on that row. Change nothing else on the row.
3. The kiosk uses the new value the next time it needs it: the next tap, menu window or scheduled job.
Rows whose What it does starts "Written by the kiosk" fill themselves in; leave them alone unless a how-to on this tab says otherwise.
Look up hours (the Hours tab)
The Hours tab shows hours, shifts and volunteers for any period you pick. It updates at about 5 AM each day; Kiosk admin > Refresh Hours updates it now.
1. Use the slicers above the tables (Year, Month, Role/Type, Activity, Volunteer) to pick a period. Every slicer filters every table.
2. In a slicer, click Clear, then tick what you want. Reload the page to clear every slicer. A sort box takes up to 20 seconds.
3. Date range: From date > Filter by condition > Greater than or equal to > a date like 2026-11-01. To date: Less than or equal to.
4. To sort a table, pick an order in the Sort box above it. Everyone sees the new order.
5. Your slicer picks are yours alone: nobody else sees them.
6. Double-click a number to see the shifts behind it on a new tab. Delete that tab when you're done.
Don't use Set current filters as default in a slicer's menu: it changes the Hours tab for everyone.
Other menu items
Kiosk admin > Refresh Hours brings the Hours tab up to date now.
Kiosk admin > Check the Log now runs the morning check for problems on the Log right away and says what it found. New problems go on the Flags tab.

Kiosk admin > Import past hours… brings shifts in from an old hours spreadsheet, from any date. Press Preview first. Running it again brings in only new rows, as long as rows it already brought in are left as they are in the old sheet and new rows go at the bottom of the tab. A shift on a day the volunteer also has a kiosk shift still comes in, flagged so you can check it isn't counted twice.
Please don't
• Rename the Log, Flags, Settings or Hours tabs. The kiosk finds them and stops working without them.
• Rename or delete the Shifts tab. The nightly auto clock-out reads it to guess when people left, and without it the guesses get worse.

• Rename a column header on the Log or Flags tab, or give two columns the same header. Adding columns of your own is fine; if one of the kiosk's columns needs to move, tell the kiosk's developers so its colours and filter views follow.
• Change a name in the Setting column on the Settings tab. The kiosk would treat that setting as missing.
• Delete a shift with a Shift ID from the Log by hand. Use Kiosk admin > Remove a shift… so a copy is kept.
• Change a Shift ID, or put one row's Shift ID on another row. Copying one to search for it is fine.
• Type over or delete anything on the Hours tab other than its slicers and Sort boxes.
• Edit the Removed shifts or Import ledger tabs by hand. The kiosk relies on them.
What the Log columns hold

Each Log and Flags column header has a hover note with the text below. Once you write your own note on a header, or change the kiosk's, the kiosk leaves it exactly as you left it, and its own text stays here. If you delete a note, the kiosk puts its own back the next time it is updated.
Date: The shift's date, as yyyy-mm-dd. Filled by the kiosk; change it only to fix a mistake.
Day: The weekday of the Date. Filled by the kiosk.
Volunteer Name: The volunteer's first and last name, from Volunteer Profiles. Filled by the kiosk; change it only to fix a mistake.
Volunteer Role/Type: Yours to fill: the volunteer's role or type. The kiosk never writes it; the Hours tab and the monthly report group by it.
Check-In Recorded (timestamp): When the volunteer actually tapped Check In on the tablet. Blank on shifts added with Kiosk admin > Add a shift… or imported.
Check-In Stated (user): The arrival time the volunteer chose on the tablet, or the time an admin entered. The same as Recorded when they chose none. Hours count from this time.
Check-Out Recorded (timestamp): When the volunteer actually tapped Check Out. Blank when an admin or the nightly auto clock-out closed the shift.
Check-Out Stated (user): The check-out time the volunteer chose, the time an admin entered, or the nightly auto clock-out's guess. Hours count to this time.
Hours Served (timestamps): Hours between the two Recorded times, to 2 decimals. For checking only: the reports don't count it.
Hours Served (stated): Hours between the two Stated times, to 2 decimals. This is what the Hours tab, the monthly report and milestones count. If you fix a time by hand, fix this too.
Admin Alerts?: The kiosk's notes when something looks off: a time far from the tap, a long shift, an unreadable time, an auto clock-out. Each one is also on the Flags tab for review.
Activity: Yours to fill: what the volunteer did. The kiosk never writes it; the Hours tab and the monthly report group by it.
Notes: Notes typed in a Kiosk admin window are added here, after anything already in the cell. Otherwise yours.
User Token: The volunteer's private token from Volunteer Profiles, which links the row to them. Keep this spreadsheet shared as narrowly as Volunteer Profiles.
Status: open from check-in until check-out, then closed. Only closed rows count toward hours.
Check-In Entered By: kiosk for a tablet check-in, an admin's initials for one added in the menu, import for past hours; blank means typed by hand.
Check-Out Entered By: kiosk, an admin's initials, auto-close for the nightly auto clock-out, or import; blank means typed by hand.
Shift ID: The row's own ID. The Kiosk admin menu and the Flags tab find the row by it, so never change it or put it on another row.
What the Flags columns hold
Date: The flagged shift's Date on the Log. Filled by the kiosk.
Volunteer Name: The flagged shift's volunteer. Filled by the kiosk.
Shift ID: The flagged shift's Shift ID: the sure way to find it on the Log (copy it, then Ctrl+F on the Log).
Reason: Why it was flagged, word for word as in the Log's Admin Alerts?, or a problem the morning Log check found.
Raised At: When the flag was raised.
Reviewed: Tick it once someone has looked at the flag. Ticked flags leave the Flags: Unreviewed view and the weekly email's unreviewed count.
Reviewed By: Yours: your initials.
Notes: Yours: what you found or did. Remove a shift and Restore a shift add a line here too.
Source: What raised it: kiosk check-in, kiosk check-out, auto-close (the nightly auto clock-out), import (Import past hours) or log check (the morning Log check).
Log Row: The Log row number when the flag was raised. A hint only: sorting the Log moves rows, so trust the Shift ID.

What it does

The code a board member types on the tablet to open the kiosk: at least 16 letters (only letters count, and capitals are the same as small letters), and while it's blank or shorter no tablet can open.
Which spreadsheet the volunteer list comes from, as the long ID in its link between /d/ and /edit; while it's blank, no volunteer can be found on the tablet or in the menu.
The tab in that spreadsheet that holds the volunteer list; blank means a tab named Volunteer Profiles.

The day the kiosk started, as yyyy-mm-dd: only volunteers who started on or after it get the first-shift welcome, and the nightly auto clock-out closes only shifts on or after it, so never leave it blank.
How many minutes a volunteer's chosen arrival time can be from the moment they tapped in before the shift is flagged, as a number 0 or more; blank means 15.
How many minutes a volunteer's chosen check-out time can be from the moment they tapped out before the shift is flagged, as a number 0 or more; blank means 15.
The dollar value of one volunteer hour, such as 34.79, used in the monthly report; while it's blank the report leaves the value out and says to set it here.
Written by the kiosk: rows of Volunteer Profiles it had to leave out, and why (blank means none), so fix them in Volunteer Profiles, not here.
How many hours after check-in a shift nobody checked out of stays open on the tablet before the nightly auto clock-out closes it, from 10 to 24; blank or anything else means 12.
Written by the kiosk: when the nightly auto clock-out last ran and how many shifts it closed, so leave it alone.
A tablet check-out that credits more hours than this is flagged as a long shift, as a number above 0; blank or anything else means 8.
Type On to send the weekly flags email; anything else, blank included, keeps it off.
Who gets the weekly flags email, as one or more email addresses separated by commas, spaces or new lines; blank sends nothing.

The weekday the weekly flags email goes out if there is anything to report, such as Monday or Mon; blank or anything else means Monday, and the first one after a change, or after turning the email On, can come sooner (see the How to tab).

The hour, Central time, the weekly flags email goes out if there is anything to report, as a whole number from 0 to 23 (8 is 8 AM, 14 is 2 PM); blank or anything else means 8, and the first one after a change, or after turning the email On, can come sooner (see the How to tab).

Written by the kiosk: when the weekly flags email last checked and whether it sent, had nothing to send or had no valid address to send to; while the email is On with an address, clearing it makes the next hourly check run again, which sends only if there is anything to report.
Written by the kiosk: the Google account that runs the nightly jobs and the weekly email, so leave it alone.
The old hours spreadsheet that Kiosk admin > Import past hours… offers first; an import fills it in, and blank just means the window starts empty.
The tab in that old hours spreadsheet that Import past hours… offers first; blank means Historical Hours.

Who to ask when the kiosk or this sheet isn't working, such as a name and an email or phone: the How to tab shows it, and so does the Kiosk admin menu when something goes wrong; while it's blank, the How to tab says to ask whoever looks after the kiosk.

Who volunteers should contact about their hours, such as a name and an email or phone: Kiosk admin > Email hours… ends every email with it, because nobody can reply to that email; while it's blank, no hours email can be sent.
Lines added under "Thank you for volunteering." in Kiosk admin > Email hours…, such as a name and a role; blank adds nothing.

Whether volunteers can ask for their hours on the tablet: Off hides the Request my hours link on the welcome screen; Approve lists requests in Kiosk admin > Email hours… for staff to send; Auto emails them every 15 minutes, skipping unchecked shifts, at most weekly; blank or anything else means Off.

Written by the hours request job: when it was installed or removed, or a run last sent, held or failed; a run with nothing to do writes nothing, so an old time is normal. In Auto, a request still waiting a day later shows as overdue in Email hours…, which is how a stopped job shows.
